<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">However, financing and/or governmental approvals have not been obtained for the hotel projects listed under &#8220;Other Signed Agreements&#8221; above, and there can be no assurances that any or all of our projects listed above will be developed as planned. If adequate project financing is not obtained, these projects may need to be limited in scope, deferred or cancelled altogether, in which case we may be unable to recover any previously funded key money, equity investments or debt financing.&nbsp;&nbsp;For example, due to our joint venture partner&#8217;s failure to achieve certain agreed milestones in the development of the Mondrian Istanbul hotel, in early 2014, we exercised our put option under the joint venture agreement and initiated foreclosure proceedings, as discussed further in note 5 of the consolidated financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Corporate Headquarters </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.06%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our corporate headquarters are located at 475 10<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">th</sup> Avenue, New York, New York, 10018. These offices consist of approximately 18,500 square feet of leased space. The lease for this property expires on October 31, 2018. We believe that our existing office properties are in good condition and are sufficient and suitable for the conduct of our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.06%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="ITEM3_LEGAL_PROCEEDINGS"></a>I<font style="font-weight:bold;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">TEM&#160;3.</font></p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:90.94%;">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><a name="ITEM3_LEGAL_PROCEEDINGS"></a>LEGAL PROCEEDINGS <font style="color:#FF0000;"> </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are involved in various lawsuits and administrative actions in the normal course of business, as well as other litigations as noted below. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Litigations Regarding Mondrian SoHo </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January&#160;16, 2013, German American Capital Corporation (&#8220;GACC&#8221; or the &#8220;lender&#8221;), the lender for the mortgage loans on Mondrian SoHo, filed a complaint in the Supreme Court of the State of New York, County of New York against Sochin Downtown Realty, LLC, the joint venture that owns Mondrian SoHo (&#8220;Sochin JV&#8221;), Morgans Management, Morgans Group, Happy Bar LLC and MGMT LLC, seeking foreclosure including, among other things, the sale of the mortgaged property free and clear of the management agreement, entered into between Sochin JV and Morgans Management on June&#160;27, 2007, as amended on July&#160;30, 2010. According to the complaint, Sochin JV defaulted by failing to repay the approximately $217 million outstanding on the loans when they became due on November&#160;15, 2012.&#160;Cape Advisors Inc. indirectly owns 80% of the equity interest in Sochin JV and Morgans Group indirectly owns the remaining 20% equity interest. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March&#160;11, 2013 we moved to dismiss the lender&#8217;s complaint on the grounds that, among other things, our management agreement is not subject to foreclosure. On April&#160;2, 2013, the lender opposed our motion to dismiss and cross-moved for summary judgment. On August&#160;12, 2013, the court heard oral argument on both motions, as well as a third motion brought by the Company to strike an affirmation submitted by lender&#8217;s attorney. On January&#160;27, 2014, the court granted Morgans Management&#8217;s motion to dismiss on the ground that Morgans Management was not a proper party to the foreclosure action and that a management contract does not constitute an interest in real property subject to foreclosure, and denied lender&#8217;s motion for summary judgment as moot.&#160;On March&#160;20, 2014 the lender moved for summary judgment against the remaining defendants,&nbsp;&nbsp;seeking foreclosure on four mortgages secured by Mondrian SoHo. By order dated May&#160;27, 2014, the trial court granted the motion for summary judgment to a limited extent, ordering the appointment of a referee to compute the amount but stating that a motion for summary judgment of foreclosure and sale is premature. By decision entered on July 28, 2014, the court referred the matter to a referee to ascertain and compute the amount due to the lender for principal, interest, and other disbursements and to determine whether the property should be sold in one parcel.&nbsp;&nbsp;On August 6, 2014, the referee set a hearing on the issues for August 18, 2014, and subsequently issued her report setting the amount due on the loan ($250.5 million, plus interest accruing at a daily rate of approximately $84,000, as of August 18, 2014) and determining the property should be sold as one parcel. On September 15, 2014, the lender filed a motion to confirm the referee&#8217;s report and for judgment of foreclosure and sale, along with the Referee&#8217;s Report of Amount Due attached as an exhibit, and a </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">38</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always">
<p style="line-height:1pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">proposed judgment of foreclosure and sale.&nbsp;&nbsp;The foreclosure judgment was issued on November 25, 2014 and the foreclosure sale was held on January 7, 2015, at which GACC was the winning and only bidder.  GACC had an agreement to assign its bid to an affiliate of the Sapir Organization (&#8220;Sapir&#8221;), a New York-based real estate development and management organization; and in connection with that contract, GACC and Sapir have agreed to terminate Morgans as manager of Mondrian SoHo.&nbsp;&nbsp;That sale to Sapir closed on March 6, 2015. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On October 24, 2014, we filed suit in the Supreme Court of the State of New York seeking a declaration that the mortgage lenders to the Mondrian SoHo debt cannot remove us as hotel manager following the conclusion of the foreclosure proceedings.&#160; The action seeks to protect and enforce our long-term hotel management contract for Mondrian SoHo, regardless of the outcome of the current foreclosure proceedings.&#160; We also seek damages against the lenders and ultimate buyer of the property should we be terminated.&#160; The lawsuit <font style="color:#000000;">does not affect the foreclosure proceedings, and we do not oppose the lenders&#8217; efforts to foreclose on the Mondrian SoHo property. On February 9, 2015, the court heard our motion for a preliminary injunction preventing the mortgage lender and/or the ultimate buyer from removing Morgans as manager of Mondrian SoHo pending resolution of the lawsuit; that motion was denied in an oral ruling that same day.&nbsp;&nbsp;While the court did not grant the injunction, it did recognize the underlying merits of our case.&nbsp;&nbsp;On February 27, 2015, we filed an appeal of the denial of our motion for a preliminary injunction in the Supreme Court of New York, Appellate Division, First Department.&nbsp;&nbsp;That appeal is currently pending.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On February&#160;25, 2013, the Sochin JV filed a complaint in the Delaware Court of Chancery against Morgans Management and Morgans Group, seeking, among other things, a declaration that Sochin JV had terminated the management agreement for the hotel.&#160;In addition, we, through our equity affiliate, filed a separate action against Sochin JV and its parent in the Delaware Court of Chancery for, among other things, breaching fiduciary duties and their joint venture agreement for failing to obtain consent prior to the termination. That action was subsequently consolidated with the joint venture&#8217;s termination action.&#160; On April&#160;30, 2013, Morgans Management filed a lawsuit against Sochin JV and the majority member of Sochin JV&#8217;s parent and its affiliate in New York Supreme Court for damages based on the wrongful attempted termination of the management agreement, defamation, and breach of fiduciary and other obligations under the parties&#8217; joint venture agreement.&#160; On September&#160;20, 2013, the Delaware Court of Chancery ruled that Sochin JV properly terminated the hotel management agreement on agency principles, that Morgans Management must vacate the hotel forthwith or on whatever other timetable the hotel owner chooses, and that certain claims by our equity affiliate are dismissed but not its breach of fiduciary duty claim.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May&#160;9, 2014, both of the above-referenced actions in Delaware and the above-referenced action in New York were dismissed with prejudice by agreement among the parties.&#160; Under the terms of the settlement, if the joint venture does not seek to remove us as manager of Mondrian SoHo prior to December 31, 2020, then we will be deemed to have released all claims against the joint venture under the Management Agreement.&#160; Under the terms of the settlement, the joint venture may demand that Morgans vacate Mondrian SoHo on 90 days&#8217; prior notice; in the event the joint venture provides notice of its intention to remove us as manager of Mondrian SoHo, all of our claims against the joint venture (including for breach of the hotel management agreement) would be revived. The joint venture&#8217;s rights under the settlement are not assignable without our written consent.&nbsp;&nbsp;In light of the sale of Mondrian SoHo to Sapir and the related litigation regarding Morgans&#8217; management of the hotel, as discussed above, we do not believe that the settlement agreement with the joint venture is relevant to our right or ability to continue to manage Mondrian SoHo.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Litigations Regarding Delano Marrakech </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.06%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2013, we served the owner of Delano Marrakech with a notice of default for numerous breaches of the management agreement, including among other things, failure to pay fees and reimbursable expenses and to operate the hotel in accordance with the standards under the management agreement. In September 2013, we served notice of termination of our management agreement for Delano Marrakech following the failure by the owner of Delano Marrakech to remedy the numerous breaches of the agreement. As a result, we discontinued all affiliation with the hotel, including removal of the Delano name, and terminated management of the property, effective November&#160;12, 2013. Pursuant to the management agreement, in the event of an owner default, we have no further obligations under the performance-based cash flow guarantee. In addition, as a result of the breaches by the hotel owner, we have asserted a claim for losses and damages against the owner that is currently estimated at in excess of $30.0 million, including interest. The owner of the hotel is disputing the circumstances surrounding termination and therefore its liability for this amount. The owner is also counterclaiming against us under both the performance-based cash flow guarantee and for loss of profits. The total counterclaim made by the owner is in excess of $119.0 million, excluding interest. We consider the counterclaim made by the owner to be entirely without merit and intend to vigorously defend ourselves while pursuing what we consider to be a strong claim against the owner. Both parties are seeking arbitration of the dispute, which is expected to occur in October 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;A preliminary hearing was heard on January 19, 2015 in which the arbitral tribunal rejected entirely the owner&#8217;s attempt to have a preliminary issue determined in its favor.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Litigation Regarding TLG Promissory Notes </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On August&#160;5, 2013, Andrew Sasson and Andy Masi filed a lawsuit in the Supreme Court of the State of New York against TLG Acquisition LLC and Morgans Group LLC relating to the $18.0&#160;million in notes convertible into shares of our common stock at $9.50 </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">39</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always">
<p style="line-height:1pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">per share subject to the achievement of certain EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) targets for the acquired TLG business (the &#8220;TLG Promissory Notes&#8221;), which were issued in connection with our November 2011 acquisition of 90% of the equity interests in a group of companies known as The Light Group (the &#8220;Light Group Transaction&#8221;) . See note 1 and note 7 of our consolidated financial statements regarding the background of the TLG Promissory Notes. The complaint alleged, among other things, a breach of contract and an event of default under the TLG Promissory Notes as a result of our failure to repay the TLG Promissory Notes following an alleged &#8220;Change of Control&#8221; that purportedly occurred upon the election of our current Board of Directors on June&#160;14, 2013. The complaint sought payment of Mr.&#160;Sasson&#8217;s $16 million TLG Promissory Note and Mr.&#160;Masi&#8217;s $2 million TLG Promissory Note, plus interest compounded to principal, as well as default interest, and reasonable costs and expenses incurred in the lawsuit. We believe that a Change of Control, within the meaning of the TLG Promissory Notes, has not occurred and that no prepayments are required under the TLG Promissory Notes. On September&#160;26, 2013, we filed a motion to dismiss the complaint in its entirety. On February&#160;6, 2014, the court granted our motion to dismiss. On March&#160;7, 2014, Messrs. Sasson and Masi filed a Notice of Appeal from this decision with the Appellate Division, First Department, and on July&#160;8, 2014, they filed their initial brief in support of that appeal. Briefing of that appeal is ongoing, and our opposition brief was due August&#160;29, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The oral argument on the motion occurred on October 29, 2014 and we are awaiting the court&#8217;s ruling. &nbsp;&nbsp;Although the TLG Promissory Notes were repaid and retired in December 2014, this lawsuit has not been dismissed.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Litigation Regarding 2013 Deleveraging Transaction, Proxy Litigation Between Mr.&#160;Burkle and OTK and Certain of Our Current Directors, and Litigation Regarding Yucaipa Board Observer Rights </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On May&#160;5, 2014, we and affiliates of Yucaipa, among other litigants, executed and submitted to the Delaware Court of Chancery the Stipulation of Settlement, which contemplated the partial settlement and dismissal of most of the defendants from the Delaware Shareholder Derivative Action and the complete settlement and dismissal of the New York Securities Action, the Proxy Action and the Board Observer Action. On July&#160;23, 2014, the Delaware Court of Chancery approved the settlement as set forth in the Settlement Stipulation, which pursuant to its terms, became effective on August 25, 2014, the Effective Date.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Settlement Stipulation provided for the partial settlement and dismissal with prejudice of most of the defendants from the action entitled <font style="font-style:italic;">OTK Associates, LLC v. Friedman</font>,<font style="font-style:italic;"> et al.</font>, C.A. No.&#160;8447-VCL (Del. Ch.) and the complete settlement and dismissal with prejudice of the actions entitled <font style="font-style:italic;">Yucaipa American Alliance Fund II L.P., et al. v. Morgans Hotel Group Co., et al.</font>, Index No.&#160;652294/2013 (NY Sup.); <font style="font-style:italic;">Burkle v. OTK Associates, LLC</font>, <font style="font-style:italic;">et al.</font>, Case No.&#160;13-CIV-4557 (S.D.N.Y.); and <font style="font-style:italic;">Yucaipa American Alliance Fund II L.P., et al. v. Morgans Hotel Group Co</font>., Index No.&#160;653455/2013 (NY Sup.),&nbsp;&nbsp;the foregoing four actions are collectively referred to as the Actions. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Settlement Stipulation provided, among other things, for the following: </p>

Our insurers covered these attorneys&#8217; fees and expenses.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

In its July&#160;23, 2014 order approving the Settlement Stipulation, the Delaware Court of Chancery awarded an aggregate amount of approximately $6.5 million (to be reduced by the prior interim award of approximately $2.7 million) to OTK and current director Jason T. <p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On October 3, 2014, we entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with OTK and Thomas L. Harrison (the &#8220;Harrison Settlement&#8221;) to settle the claims against Mr. Harrison in the Delaware Shareholder Derivative Action and also to settle claims Mr. Harrison has asserted against us in <font style="font-style:italic;">Harrison v. Morgans Hotel Group Co.,</font> C. A. No. 10100-VCL (Del. Ch.) (the &#8220;Harrison Advancement Action&#8221;), in which Mr. Harrison seeks an order requiring us to advance his expenses (including attorneys&#8217; fees) incurred in connection with the Delaware Shareholder Derivative Action and further seeks indemnification of the expenses (including attorneys&#8217; fees) Mr. Harrison incurred in connection with his efforts to enforce his claims to advancement.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Harrison Settlement is subject to approval by the Delaware Court of Chancery.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to the Harrison Settlement, in October 2014, we advanced to Mr. Harrison a portion of the fees and expenses for which he has sought advancement and paid a portion of the amounts for which Mr. Harrison seeks indemnification related to the Harrison Advancement Action. &#160;As part of the consideration for the release of the claims against Mr. Harrison in the Delaware Shareholder Derivative Action, if the Harrison Settlement is approved by the Court of Chancery, Mr. Harrison would waive his claims to recover the remaining amounts for which he has sought advancement and indemnification in the Harrison Advancement Action.&nbsp;&nbsp;On November 7, 2014, OTK, Morgans, and Mr. Harrison entered into a Stipulation of Settlement setting forth the terms of the settlement. The settlement hearing before the Delaware Court of Chancery was held on February 9, 2015, and the Court of Chancery approved the Harrison Settlement.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, both the Harrison Advancement Action and the claims against Mr. Harrison in the Delaware Shareholder Derivative Action were dismissed with prejudice and the parties to the settlement exchanged customary releases.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the Harrison Settlement, OTK and Morgans informed the Delaware Court of Chancery that if the Harrison Settlement were approved, OTK intended to seek dismissal of the claims against the only remaining defendant in the Delaware Shareholder Derivative Action, Michael D. Malone, a former director of the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;On February 17, 2015, the remaining parties to the litigation filed a stipulation and proposed form of order to dismiss the claims against Mr. Malone without prejudice, and the Court entered the dismissal order on February 18, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Delaware Shareholder Derivative Action is now concluded. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our insurers have paid a majority of the costs that we were obligated to pay under the Settlement Stipulation.&nbsp;&nbsp;We do not expect that the net amount of any remaining payments we will make under the terms of the Settlement Stipulation or in connection with the Harrison Settlement or the Malone dismissal will be material to our financial position. </p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="PART_II"></a>PART II </p>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">

<td valign="top" style="width:9.06%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ITEM&#160;5.</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:90.94%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><a name="ITEM5_MARKET_FOR_REGISTRANT"></a><font style="font-style:italic;">MARKET FOR REGISTRANT&#8217;S COMMON EQUITY, RELATED STOCKHOLDER MATTERS AND ISSUER PURCHASES OF EQUITY SECURITIES</font> </p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Market Information </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our common stock has been listed on the NASDAQ Global Market under the symbol &#8220;MHGC&#8221; since the completion of our initial public offering in February 2006. <p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On Ma<font style="color:#000000;">rch&#160;12, 2015,</font> the closing sale price for our common stock, as reported on the NASDAQ Global Market, was<font style="color:#000000;"> $7.21. </font>As of <font style="color:#000000;">March&#160;12, 2015,</font> there w<font style="color:#000000;">ere 37 record hol</font>ders of our common stock, although there is a much larger number of beneficial owners. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Dividend Policy </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have never declared or paid any cash dividends on our common stock and we do not currently intend to pay any cash dividends on our common stock. We expect to retain future earnings, if any, to fund the development and growth of our business. Any future determination to pay dividends on our common stock will be, subject to applicable law, at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend upon, among other factors, our results of operations, financial condition, capital requirements and contractual restrictions. Our Hudson/Delano 2014 Mortgage Loan prohibits us from paying cash dividends on our common stock. In addition, so long as any Series A preferred securities are outstanding, we are prohibited from paying dividends on our common stock, unless all accumulated and unpaid dividends on all outstanding Series A preferred securities have been declared and paid in full. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Series A preferred securities we issued in October 2009 had an 8% dividend rate until October 2014, and have a 10% dividend rate until October 2016, and a 20% dividend rate thereafter, with a 4% increase in the dividend rate during certain periods in which the Yucaipa Investors&#8217; nominee to our Board of Directors has not been elected as a director or subsequently appointed as a director by our Board of Directors. The cumulative unpaid dividends also have a dividend rate equal to the then applicable dividend rate on the Series A preferred securities. We have the option to accrue any and all dividend payments, and as of December&#160;31, 2014, have not declared any dividends. As of December&#160;31, 2014, we have undeclared dividends of approximately $43.3 million. </p>

<td valign="top" style="width:95.46%;">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;color:#;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Symbol';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">our investments in certain hotels under development and other proposed properties. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Effective<font style="color:#000000;"> January 23, 2015, w</font>e completed the TLG Equity Sale, as discussed in <font style="color:#000000;">Item&#160;1 of Part&#160;I of this report under the heading </font> &#8220;2014 Key Events and Other Recent Transactions and Developments.&#8221; Also, effective March 6, 2015, we no longer hold any equity interest in Mondrian SoHo.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our corporate strategy is to achieve growth as a boutique hotel management and brand company by leveraging our management experience and one-of-a-kind luxury brands for expansion into major gateway markets and key resort destinations in both domestic and international markets. We intend to achieve growth primarily through the pursuit of new long-term management agreements and, in select situations where we believe third-party managers have the experience and resources to satisfy our high branding standards, franchise or licensing agreements. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additionally, we also intend to enhance the value of our existing hotels and management agreements through targeted renovation and expansion projects. We believe that by pursuing this targeted strategy, while remaining open and flexible to unique opportunities, we will strengthen our position as a leader in lifestyle hospitality management. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management, Franchise, and License Agreements.<font style="font-style:normal;"> Although our hotel management agreements and franchise or license agreements are generally long-term, they may be subject to early termination in specified circumstances, or we may agree to early termination as circumstances require. Certain of our hotel management agreements and franchise or license agreements contain performance tests that stipulate certain minimum levels of operating performance,</font><font style="font-style:normal;color:#000000;"> which could result in early termination of our hotel management, license or franchise agreements, once the performance test period begins, which is generally multiple years after a hotel opens. As of December 31, 2014, we are in compliance with these termination performance tests and are not exercising any contractual cure rights.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-style:normal;">We may disagree with hotel owners on how the performance criteria are calculated or whether they have been met. In addition, some courts have applied principles of agency law and related fiduciary standards to managers of third-party hotel </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">46</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always">
<p style="line-height:1pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-style:normal;">properties (or have interpreted hotel management agreements as &#8220;personal services contracts&#8221;). This means, among other things, that property owners may assert the right to terminate management agreements even where the agreements provide otherwise, and some courts have upheld such assertions regarding management agreements and may do so in the future. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Several of our hotels are also subject to mortgage and mezzanine debt, and in some instances our management, franchise or license fee is subordinated to the debt. Some of our management agreements also may be terminated by the lenders on foreclosure or certain other related events. With some of our existing management, franchise and license agreements we have negotiated, and with all of our new management, franchise and license agreements for hotels under development we attempt to negotiate, non-disturbance agreements or similar protections with the mortgage lender, or to require that such agreements be entered into upon securing of financing, in order to protect our agreements in the event of foreclosure.&#160;However, we are not always successful in imposing these requirements, and some of our new development projects and existing hotels do not have non-disturbance or similar protections, which may make the related agreements subject to termination by the lenders on foreclosure or certain other related events.&#160;Even if we have such non-disturbance protections in place, they may be subject to conditions and may be difficult or costly to enforce in a foreclosure situation. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We may also terminate hotel management, franchise or license agreements as circumstances require or as we deem appropriate. For example, in September 2014, we and the hotel owners mutually agreed to terminate the Delano Moscow management agreement and, as a result, we were relieved of our key money and possible cash flow commitment obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="color:#000000;">Additionally, in June 2014, the Mondrian at Baha Mar management agreement was terminated due to the failure of the hotel owner to obtain a non-disturbance agreement from its lender as required by the management agreement, among other things.&nbsp;&nbsp; This termination relieved us of a $10.0 million key money obligation.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Joint Ventures and Non-Wholly Owned Entities.<font style="font-style:normal;"> We own partial interests in the Joint Venture Hotels and the F&amp;B Venture. We account for these investments using the equity method as we believe we do not exercise control over significant asset decisions such as buying, selling or financing nor are we the primary beneficiary of the entities. Under the equity method, we increase our investment in unconsolidated joint ventures for our proportionate share of net income and contributions and decrease our investment balance for our proportionate share of net losses and distributions. Once our investment balance in an unconsolidated joint venture is zero, we suspend recording additional losses. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;color:#;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;<font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations </font></p>

Through our prior ownership of TLG, we recognized management fees in accordance with the applicable management agreement, which generally provided for base management fees as a percentage of gross sales, and incentive management fees as a percentage of net profits, as calculated pursuant to the management agreements. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">47</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always">
<p style="line-height:1pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fluctuations in revenues, which tend to correlate with changes in gross domestic product, are driven largely by general economic and local economic conditions but can also be impacted by major events, such as terrorist attacks or natural disasters, which in turn affect levels of business and leisure travel. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Renovations at our hotels can have a significant impact on our revenues. For example, our guest room and corridor renovations at Hudson, which began in the fourth quarter of 2011 and were completed in late 2012, had a material impact on our operating results during the year ended December&#160;31, 2012. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The seasonal nature of the hospitality business can also impact revenues. For example, our Miami hotels are generally strongest in the first quarter, whereas our New York hotels are generally strongest in the fourth quarter. However, prevailing economic conditions can cause fluctuations which impact seasonality. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition to economic conditions, supply is another important factor that can affect revenues. Room rates, occupancy and food and beverage revenues tend to fall when supply increases, unless the supply growth is offset by an equal or greater increase in demand. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Finally, competition within the hospitality industry can affect revenues. Competitive factors in the hospitality industry include name recognition, quality of service, convenience of location, quality of the property or venue, pricing, and range and quality of nightlife, food and beverage services and amenities offered.  We also compete with other operators, including major hospitality chains with well-established and recognized brands.&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="color:#000000;">Our competitors generally also have broader guest loyalty programs which may enable them to attract more customers and more effectively retain such guests. </font>In addition, all of our hotels, restaurants, nightclubs, and bars are located in areas where there are numerous competitors, many of whom have substantially greater financial and marketing resources than us. New or existing competitors could offer significantly lower rates and pricing or more convenient locations, services or amenities or significantly expand, improve or introduce new service offerings in markets in which our hotels, restaurants, nightclubs, bars, and other food and beverage venues compete, thereby posing a greater competitive threat than at present. If we are unable to compete effectively, we would lose market share, which could adversely affect our revenues.  </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating Costs and Expenses. <font style="font-style:normal;">Our operating costs and expenses consist of the costs to provide hotel and food and beverage services, costs to operate our hotel management company, costs to operate our TLG food and beverage company prior to the TLG Equity Sale, and costs associated with the ownership of our assets, including: </font></p>

We also record amortization on our other assets, such as the three restaurant leases in Las Vegas that we purchased in August 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Prior to classifying TLG as held for sale in December 2014, </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;color:#000000;">we reco</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">rded amortization expense related to the TLG management contracts we acquired as part of our acquisition of TLG in November 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

In this analysis of fair value, we use discounted cash flow analysis to estimate the fair value of our investment taking into account expected cash flow from operations, holding period and net proceeds from the dispositions of the property. Any decline that is not expected to be recovered is considered other-than-temporary and an impairment charge is recorded as a reduction in the carrying value of the investment. </font></p></td></tr></table></div>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;color:#;font-family:'Symbol';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#183;</p></td>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Most categories of variable operating expenses, such as operating supplies, and certain labor, such as housekeeping, fluctuate with changes in occupancy. Increases in RevPAR attributable to increases in occupancy are accompanied by increases in most categories of variable operating costs and expenses. Increases in RevPAR attributable to improvements in ADR typically only result in increases in limited categories of operating costs and expenses, primarily credit card and travel agent commissions. Thus, improvements in ADR have a more significant impact on improving our operating margins than occupancy. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">49</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always">
<p style="line-height:1pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;<font style="font-size:10pt;">Notwithstanding our efforts to reduce variable costs, there are limits to how much we can reduce total costs because we have significant costs that are relatively fixed costs, such as depreciation and amortization, labor costs and employee benefits, insurance, real estate taxes, interest and other expenses associated with owning hotels that do not necessarily decrease when circumstances such as market factors cause a reduction in our hotel revenues. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent Trends and Developments </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent Trends. &nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="font-style:normal;color:#000000;">Lodging demand is closely linked to the performance of the general economy and is sensitive to business and personal discretionary spending levels.  Declines in consumer demand due to adverse general economic conditions, risks reducing travel patterns, lower consumer confidence and adverse political conditions can lower the revenues and profitability of our Owned Hotels and limit the amount of fee revenues we are able to generate from our Managed Hotels and franchised properties.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additionally, <font style="color:#;">the pace of new lodging supply, especially in New York City and Miami, has increased over the past several years as many projects initiated before the economic downturn came to fruition and new projects commenced as the economy recovered. </font>In New York City and South Beach, new lodging supply impacted our hotels&#8217; occupancy and constrained rate growth, and we expect that these trends will continue through 2015 as the new supply in these markets is absorbed.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.13%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also believe the impact of the strong U.S. dollar and a weak global economy, specifically in Europe, could impact our hotels in New York City and Miami in 2015, where we are particularly dependent on international tourists.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Rev<font style="color:#;">PAR at System-Wide Comparable Hotels, all of which are located in the United States and includes all Morgans Hotel Group branded hotels operated by us, except for hotels added or under major renovation during the current or the prior year, development projects and hotels no longer managed by us, increased by 2.8% in 2014 as compared to 2013, driven by a 1.8% increase in occupancy and 1.0% increase in ADR.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RevPAR from System-Wide Comparable Hotels in New York decreased 0.2% in 2014 over 2013, due to decreased ADR of 1.4%.&nbsp;&nbsp;Occupancy at our New York hotels was strong at 89.7% in 2014, an increase of 1.2% as compared to 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;RevPAR at Hudson decreased by 1.0% during 2014 as compared to 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Occupancy at Hudson increased by 2.1% to 90.9% year-over-year  and ADR at Hudson declined 3.0% during 2014, primarily as a result of an increase in competitive room supply. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">RevPAR from System-Wide Comparable Hotels in Miami increased 2.1% in 2014 as compared to 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;Delano South Beach experienced a RevPAR increase of 2.1% during 2014 as compared to 2013 primarily due to increased occupancy year-over-year.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our System-Wide Comparable Hotels on the West Coast generated 11.5% RevPAR growth in 2014 as compared to 2013, with a 9.7% RevPAR increase at Clift.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our managed hotels in London, Sanderson, St Martins Lane and Mondrian London, are non-comparable between 2014 and 2013 due to a major renovation of Sanderson and St Martins Lanes&#8217; guestrooms and public spaces, and the opening <font style="color:#000000;">of Mondrian London on September 30, 2014. </font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Calibri;color:#000000;"> </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent Developments. <font style="font-style:normal;">In addition to the recent trends described above, we expect that a number of recent events will cause our future results of operations to differ from our historical performance. For a discussion of these recent events, see Part I, &#8220;Item 1. &#8220;Business &#8211; Key Events and Other Recent Transactions and Developments.&#8221; </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Total Hotel Revenues. <font style="font-style:normal;">Total hotel revenues increased 1.2% to $212.2 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $209.8 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. </font><font style="font-style:normal;color:#000000;">This increase was primarily due to increased occupancy at our Owned Hotels.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Rooms revenue <font style="font-style:normal;">increased 2.4% to $123.8 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $120.8 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to increases in occupancy at Delano South Beach and increases in occupancy and ADR at Clift in San Francisco during year ended December 31, 2014 as compared to the same period in 2013. </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Food and beverage revenue <font style="font-style:normal;">decreased 2.2% to $82.2 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $84.1 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This decrease was primarily due to a decrease of approximately $10.4 million related to the&nbsp;&nbsp;transfer of the food and beverage venues at St Martins Lane in London to the hotel owner effective January&#160;1, 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Offsetting this decrease was an increase of approximately $5.9 million from our three leased food and beverage venues at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, one of which opened in February 2013 and another restaurant which opened in July 2013. Additionally, we saw an increase in revenues of approximately $2.6 million at the food and beverage venues at Hudson, primarily Hudson Common, which opened in February 2013. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other hotel revenue <font style="font-style:normal;">increased 28.0% to $6.2 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $4.9 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to increased internet revenues at Hudson during 2014 as compared to the same period in 2013, which was the result of a change in strategy regarding internet pricing that became effective January&#160;1, 2014, and an urban resort fee implemented at Delano South Beach and Hudson in the latter half of 2014.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management Fee&#8212;Related Parties and Other Income. <font style="font-style:normal;">Management fee&#8212;related parties and other income decreased by 14.9% to $22.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $26.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. Approximately $2.3 million of this decrease was due to a termination fees related to Hotel Las Palapas and Ames that we received during 2013. Excluding one-time items, management fees primarily decreased as a result of a decrease in fees from TLG primarily due to revisions in the management fee structure with MGM effective January&#160;1, 2014. Additionally, we experienced a decrease in management fees from managed hotels, primarily due to the loss of the Ames management contract, major renovations at Sanderson and St Martins Lane which began during the first quarter of 2014, and lower technical service fees.</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:8pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating Costs and Expenses </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Rooms expense<font style="font-style:normal;"> was relatively flat at $37.3 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $36.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This slight increase is less than the&nbsp;&nbsp;percentage increase in rooms revenue, discussed above, due to restructuring initiatives implemented on May&#160;1, 2014 at our hotel properties.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Food and beverage expense <font style="font-style:normal;">decreased 2.1% to $60.4 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $61.8 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This decrease is consistent with the decrease in food and beverage revenue, discussed above, and is primarily due to decrease in food and beverage expenses related to the effective transfer of the food and beverage venues at St Martins Lane in London to the hotel owner on January&#160;1, 2014. Offsetting these decreases were increased expenses associated with the three leased food and beverage venues at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas and at the food and beverage venues at Hudson, primarily Hudson Common. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other departmental expense <font style="font-style:normal;">was relatively flat at $3.3 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014 and December&#160;31, 2013. A slight increase of 1.5% was primarily the result of increased expenses at Hudson related to the change in internet pricing strategy discussed above.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Hotel selling, general and administrative expense <font style="font-style:normal;">decreased 5.0% to $41.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $43.9 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This decrease was primarily due to a decrease in advertising and promotional expenses due to cost-control measures taken in 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Property taxes, insurance and other expense <font style="font-style:normal;">decreased 4.6% to $16.5 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $17.3 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This decrease was primarily due to real estate tax refunds received at Delano South Beach during the second quarter of 2014 and Clift during the third quarter of 2014 for which there was no comparable refunds received during the same periods in 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">52</p>

<hr style="page-break-after:always">
<p style="line-height:1pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Corporate expenses, including stock compensation <font style="font-style:normal;">decreased 5.8% to $26.0 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $27.6 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This decrease was primarily due to savings resulting from the Termination Plan in March 2014 that resulted in a workforce reduction of our corporate office employees, which was partially offset by a $1.5 million litigation settlement at TLG in 2014. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Depreciation and amortization <font style="font-style:normal;">increased 5.5% to $28.9 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $27.4 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to the increased depreciation related to the renovation of certain food and beverage outlets at Hudson in 2013 and 2014 and the conversion of SROs into new guest rooms at Hudson in early 2014.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restructuring and disposal costs <font style="font-style:normal;">increased 26.9% to $14.5 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $11.5 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to severance and related costs incurred in early 2014 relating to the Termination Plan. Costs incurred during 2013 primarily related to legal and advisory fees incurred in connection with the 2013 Deleveraging Transaction, discussed further in </font><font style="font-style:normal;color:#000000;">note 7 to </font><font style="font-style:normal;">our consolidated financial statements. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Development costs <font style="font-style:normal;">increased 57.6% to $4.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $3.0 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to costs incurred in 2014 related to the termination of the management agreement for Mondrian at Baha Mar, including the write-off of capitalized costs, and costs associated with the initiation of foreclosure proceedings related to Mondrian Istanbul, as discussed further in note 5 to our consolidated financial statements. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Impairment loss on receivables and other assets from unconsolidated joint venture and managed hotel<font style="font-style:normal;"> was zero for the year ended December 31, 2014 compared to $6.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2013. During 2013, we impaired certain outstanding receivables due from Mondrian SoHo and Delano Marrakech, as management concluded that collection of these receivables was uncertain, and we impaired the balance of our key money investment in Delano Marrakech. There were no comparable impairment charges in 2014. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;<font style="font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Interest expense, net </font><font style="font-size:10pt;">increased 18.1% to $54.3 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to $46.0 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to a $2.2 million exit fee related to the repayment of the Hudson 2012 Mortgage Loan in February 2014, defined below in &#8220;<strike>--</strike>Debt&#8221;, and the Hudson/Delano 2014 Mortgage Loan, which closed in February 2014, resulting in a larger debt balance outstanding during 2014 as compared the same period in 2013. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Equity in (income) loss of unconsolidated joint ventures <font style="font-style:normal;">resulted in a slight gain for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 compared to a loss of $0.8 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. We no longer record our share of equity losses on a majority of our unconsolidated joint ventures, as we have written our investment balances down to zero due to impairments recorded in prior periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gain on asset sales <font style="font-style:normal;">was flat for the periods presented, resulting in income of $8.0 million for the years ended December&#160;31, 2014 and 2013. This income was related to the recognition of gains we recorded on the sales of Royalton, Morgans and Mondrian Los Angeles and our 50% ownership in the entity that owned Sanderson and St Martins Lane, all occurring in 2011. As we have significant continuing involvement with these hotels through long-term management agreements, the gains on sales are deferred and recognized over the initial term of the related management agreement. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other non-operating expenses <font style="font-style:normal;">increased 37.0% to $3.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 as compared to $2.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to settlement and litigation related costs incurred in 2014. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income tax expen<font style="color:#000000;">se </font><font style="font-style:normal;color:#000000;">increased to $1.5 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2014 as compared to $0.7 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013. This increase was primarily due to recognition of additional valuation allowance against a portion of the deferred tax assets that we believed was more likely than not to be unrealized.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><br></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">53</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&nbsp;</p></td>

<td valign="bottom"  BGCOLOR="#FFFFFF" style="padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;width:1%; border-bottom:solid 0.75pt transparent;white-space:nowrap;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">)%</p></td>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Total Hotel Revenues. <font style="font-style:normal;">Total hotel revenues increased 26.9% to $209.8 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013 compared to $165.3 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2012. This increase was primarily due to the impact of renovations at Delano South Beach and Hudson during 2012. Delano South Beach was under renovation during the first quarter of 2012, and Hudson was under significant renovation for the entire year of 2012, which negatively impacted the operating results at these hotels in the prior year. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Rooms revenue <font style="font-style:normal;">increased 17.8% to $120.8 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013 compared to $102.5 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2012. This increase was primarily due to the impact in 2012 of renovations at Delano South Beach and Hudson, discussed above, and strong operating trends in New York and San Francisco resulting in increases in occupancy and strong operating trends in Miami South Beach resulting in higher ADR in 2013. </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>

<td valign="bottom"  BGCOLOR="#CFF0FC" style="padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;padding-Bottom:0pt;width:1%;white-space:nowrap;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">%</p></td>
